recommendation: Keep the audit commit as-is. Do not restore the older literal wording for FHIR-5406, because FHIR-28589 deliberately replaced it with the current behavior-focused wording.
issue_request: FHIR-5406 was a Published/Persuasive DSTU1 FHIR-core-search ballot comment asking the search page to state that servers should repeat the original _count parameter in returned page links so subsequent paging requests honor the original _count.
initial_application: Jira comments cite SVN revisions 4496 and 4497. Git-svn commit 354ab48017ef928149f648f6c2e7e77f697afd69, build@4496, added the requested _count page-link sentence to source/search.html on 2015-03-14.
additional_context: Later Published issue FHIR-28589 revisited the same sentence for requests where _count exceeds a server maximum page size. Its resolution and application changed the literal 'repeat the original _count parameter' wording to the current behavior-focused guidance: pages reachable via links should respect the original requested _count expectations or a server-overridden max page size. A 2020 Zulip thread supports that later clarification, and corrected FHIR-5406-specific Zulip and Confluence searches found no conflicting community evidence.
reconciliation: No source change was made. source/search.html remains the active search page and currently tells servers not to return more matching resources in a single page than requested and to ensure linked pages respect the original requested _count expectations or server max page size, which satisfies FHIR-5406 when interpreted with FHIR-28589.

related_jiras.note: Published clarification of the same _count page-link sentence changed literal parameter repetition to respecting original _count expectations or server max page size.
